- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67 over recent days) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices — reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to peak sentiment period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day average), model often overshoots — apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.33) or shows strong downward momentum, model frequently underestimates — increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or risk aversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes during high news volume periods — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% if news volume >2.5 (normalized) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts — if sentiment change >0.5 in last 3 days, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect momentum.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly positive (0.33–0.67) and news volume is low, model tends to underestimate — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for hidden volatility or delayed reaction.
